plain: A researcher who goes by Luke Caverns says that Luis Alvarez, a physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project, the US wartime effort to build the atomic bomb, took a team to Egypt in the 1960s. He says they scanned the Khafre pyramid at Giza, using muons, tiny particles from space that pass through rock and can reveal hidden chambers. The podcast host Jesse Michels tells it twice, once saying Alvarez x-rayed the pyramids in the 1950s and once placing it in the 1970s, and neither time does he name the pyramid. People tell it because, if true, it shows a top nuclear scientist was searching the pyramids for hidden spaces.
